passages.provision_quote: (b) (1) A person, committee, or other entity shall not, during the time period set forth in subdivision (c), with malice, knowingly distribute an advertisement or other election communication containing materially deceptive content of any of the following:
passages.note: Bill prohibits persons/committees from distributing deceptive AI election media and explicitly exempts interactive computer services (platforms) from liability; it does not require platforms to remove or label content, so it does not speak to the platform-responsibility dimension the rungs separate.

rows.reasoning: The only source is AB 2839 (2023-2024), which Pellerin authored. Its operative clause bars persons, committees, and entities from knowingly distributing materially deceptive election media, and subdivision (e)(4) explicitly exempts interactive computer services from liability under the section. None of the rungs' clauses (platforms required to remove false information, platforms required to label content, voluntary standards for platforms, protecting free speech/preventing government censorship, or banning government involvement in content moderation) are addressed, since this bill neither mandates nor forbids platform content-moderation action. It is adjacent to the topic, not on-question for the served rungs.
needs_source: Pellerin's own words or a record speaking directly to platform content-moderation duties (removal mandates, labeling requirements, voluntary standards, or anti-censorship/free-speech protections for platforms)
